# Gomory-Hu Tree

## Definition

Let $G = (V, E)$ be an undirected graph with capacity function $u : E(G) \to \mathbb{R}_+$. A **Gomory-Hu tree** for $(G, u)$ is a weighted tree $T = (V, F)$ on the same vertex set $V$, with edge weights $w : F \to \mathbb{R}_+$, satisfying the following two properties.

## Property 1 (Cut-equivalence / minimum-cut value preservation)

For every pair of distinct vertices $s, t \in V$, the value of the **minimum $s$-$t$ cut** in $G$ equals the minimum edge weight along the unique path $P_T(s,t)$ connecting $s$ and $t$ in $T$:

$$\lambda_{st} \;=\; \min_{e \in P_T(s,t)} w(e).$$

Here $\lambda_{st}$ denotes the **minimum cut value** separating $s$ from $t$ in $G$, i.e.

$$\lambda_{st} \;=\; \min_{\substack{C \subseteq V \\ s \in C,\; t \notin C}} u\bigl(\delta_G(C)\bigr),$$

which, by the max-flow min-cut theorem, also equals the maximum $s$-$t$ flow value in $G$.

## Property 2 (Cut-realization / each tree edge induces a genuine minimum cut)

For every edge $e \in F(T)$, let $C_e \subseteq V$ be one of the two connected components of $T - e$ (so removing $e$ from $T$ partitions $V$ into $C_e$ and $V \setminus C_e$). Then the edge cut

$$\delta_G(C_e) \;=\; \bigl\{ \{x,y\} \in E(G) : x \in C_e,\; y \notin C_e \bigr\}$$

is a **minimum cut** in $G$ separating the two endpoints of $e$. Concretely, if $e = \{s,t\}$, then

$$u\bigl(\delta_G(C_e)\bigr) \;=\; w(e) \;=\; \lambda_{st}.$$

In words: the capacity of the cut $\delta_G(C_e)$ in $G$ equals the weight $w(e)$ assigned to tree edge $e$, and this cut is a minimum $s$-$t$ cut for the endpoints of $e$.

## Notation summary

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| $\lambda_{st}$ | The minimum $s$-$t$ cut value in $G$; equivalently the maximum $s$-$t$ flow value. |
| $\delta_G(C_e)$ | The set of edges of $G$ crossing the partition $(C_e, V\setminus C_e)$, i.e. $\{xy \in E(G) : x \in C_e,\, y \notin C_e\}$. Its capacity $u(\delta_G(C_e)) = \sum_{f \in \delta_G(C_e)} u(f)$. |
| $C_e$ | One connected component of $T - e$; the vertex set on one side of the cut induced by removing tree edge $e$. |
| $w(e)$ | The weight of tree edge $e$ in $T$, equal to $u(\delta_G(C_e)) = \lambda_{st}$ for the endpoints $s,t$ of $e$. |

## Why both properties matter

Property 2 guarantees that every edge of $T$ corresponds to a *real* minimum cut of $G$ (not just a number). Property 1 then extends this to *all* pairs: the minimum cut value for any pair $s,t$ is read off from the bottleneck edge on the $T$-path between them, even though that bottleneck edge's induced cut may not itself separate $s$ from $t$. Together they say $T$ is a **compact representation of all $|V|\choose 2$ pairwise minimum-cut values** using only $|V|-1$ cuts, and each of those $|V|-1$ cuts is an actual minimum cut of $G$.

## Existence

Gomory and Hu (1961) proved that such a tree always exists for any undirected graph with nonnegative capacities, and it can be constructed using at most $|V|-1$ max-flow computations via a recursive splitting procedure.
